It was a warm day. I left Richard in the kitchen whilst I went into the hall on my way to the bathroom. In the hall was my grandmother's handbag, lying open on the hall table, with her purse just visible within. There was nobody around in the hall except me, so I nervously opened her purse and took out some money, quickly stuffing it into my pocket before closing the purse again and going into the toilet.</p><p>Once I was done, I went back into the kitchen where Richard was waiting. He also needed to go to the toilet. Whilst waiting for him, my grandmother came into the kitchen. I jumped, spoke nervously to her and just as I was getting scared, Richard came back in, so I told my gran we were going outside again and left.</p><p>Once outside, I said we should go to the toy shop anyway and see what they had. We got on our bicycles and headed over; a ride of about ten minutes. On the way, I told him that I had managed to find enough money to buy us some more ammunition for our spud guns. he was excited by this and very happy that we could continue our game.</p><p>We got into the shop, bought several strips of caps and left. I gave half the ammunition to Richard and we loaded up. The next twenty minutes or so found us engrossed in a game of shooting at imaginary foes, at each other and at a couple of other kids. Then we were out of ammunition again. It was also time to go home.</p><p><br></p><p>I said goodbye to Richard and went into my house, as he went into his. Once inside I was called into the living room and asked what we'd been doing. I was still excited by our game, so explained that we had been playing with our guns. I faltered a bit as I said we had bought some extra caps for them, but then said Richard had paid for them. </p><p>My gran looked at me and asked where we'd got the money, as she knew I hadn't had any, and neither would Richard have had any pocket money (we got pocket money on Fridays and this was a Thursday).</p><p>I told her I didn't know. She then said her handbag had been tampered with, the purse not being in its normal place, and there was some money missing. Did I know anything about this? </p><p><br></p><p>I told her I hadn't touched it and didn't know who would. I also told her Richard had been alone in the hall, so she should ask him if he knew.</p><p><br></p><p>Before I knew it, my gran had grabbed my arm and dragged me across to Richard's house, where she knocked on the door. It was a warm day. I left Richard in the kitchen whilst I went into the hall on my way to the bathroom. In the hall was my grandmother's handbag, lying open on the hall table, with her purse just visible within. There was nobody around in the hall except me, so I nervously opened her purse and took out some money, quickly stuffing it into my pocket before closing the purse again and going into the toilet.</p><p>Once I was done, I went back into the kitchen where Richard was waiting. He also needed to go to the toilet. Whilst waiting for him, my grandmother came into the kitchen. I jumped, spoke nervously to her and just as I was getting scared, Richard came back in, so I told my gran we were going outside again and left.</p><p>Once outside, I said we should go to the toy shop anyway and see what they had. We got on our bicycles and headed over; a ride of about ten minutes. On the way, I told him that I had managed to find enough money to buy us some more ammunition for our spud guns. he was excited by this and very happy that we could continue our game.</p><p>We got into the shop, bought several strips of caps and left. I gave half the ammunition to Richard and we loaded up. The next twenty minutes or so found us engrossed in a game of shooting at imaginary foes, at each other and at a couple of other kids. Then we were out of ammunition again. It was also time to go home.</p><p><br></p><p>I said goodbye to Richard and went into my house, as he went into his. Once inside I was called into the living room and asked what we'd been doing. I was still excited by our game, so explained that we had been playing with our guns. I faltered a bit as I said we had bought some extra caps for them, but then said Richard had paid for them. </p><p>My gran looked at me and asked where we'd got the money, as she knew I hadn't had any, and neither would Richard have had any pocket money (we got pocket money on Fridays and this was a Thursday).</p><p>I told her I didn't know. She then said her handbag had been tampered with, the purse not being in its normal place, and there was some money missing. There was nobody around in the hall except me, so I nervously opened her purse and took out some money, quickly stuffing it into my pocket before closing the purse again and going into the toilet.</p><p>Once I was done, I went back into the kitchen where Richard was waiting. He also needed to go to the toilet. Whilst waiting for him, my grandmother came into the kitchen. I jumped, spoke nervously to her and just as I was getting scared, Richard came back in, so I told my gran we were going outside again and left.</p><p>Once outside, I said we should go to the toy shop anyway and see what they had. We got on our bicycles and headed over; a ride of about ten minutes. On the way, I told him that I had managed to find enough money to buy us some more ammunition for our spud guns. he was excited by this and very happy that we could continue our game.</p><p>We got into the shop, bought several strips of caps and left. I gave half the ammunition to Richard and we loaded up. The next twenty minutes or so found us engrossed in a game of shooting at imaginary foes, at each other and at a couple of other kids. Then we were out of ammunition again. It was also time to go home.</p><p><br></p><p>I said goodbye to Richard and went into my house, as he went into his. Once inside I was called into the living room and asked what we'd been doing. I was still excited by our game, so explained that we had been playing with our guns. I faltered a bit as I said we had bought some extra caps for them, but then said Richard had paid for them. </p><p>My gran looked at me and asked where we'd got the money, as she knew I hadn't had any, and neither would Richard have had any pocket money (we got pocket money on Fridays and this was a Thursday).</p><p>I told her I didn't know. She then said her handbag had been tampered with, the purse not being in its normal place, and there was some money missing. Did I know anything about this? </p><p><br></p><p>I told her I hadn't touched it and didn't know who would. I also told her Richard had been alone in the hall, so she should ask him if he knew.</p><p><br></p><p>Before I knew it, my gran had grabbed my arm and dragged me across to Richard's house, where she knocked on the door.
